newsitem.title: USA: U.S. approves $14 billion Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. approves $14 billion Boeing merger.

text.p: The U.S. Government on Tuesday unconditionally approved the $14 billion merger of Boeing Co. and McDonnell DouglaS, helping clear the way for creation of the world's largest aircraft maker.

The Federal Trade Commission approval required no changes to the deal, an FTC spokeswoman said. Attention now turns to Brussels, where the European Union is due to decide this month whether to approve the combination.
Critics have expressed concern the merger will narrow the playing field for commercial aircraft from three firms to two, Boeing and the European consortium, Airbus Industrie.

But the FTC said in a statement announcing its decision that McDonnell Douglas was no longer a competitive force in the aircraft market. The FTC did, however, back the EU view that Boeing's exclusive provider contracts to airlines were "potentially troubling."

European Union Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said this spring the merger could not be approved as long as Boeing continued its exclusive sales agreements with Delta Airlines, American Airlines and Continental Airlines.
On Friday, EU competition authorities will share their proposed recommendations on the Boeing deal in a closed meeting with competition authorities from the 15 EU member nations.
